questions.question: What is the main purpose of a simple machine?
choices: Change the size or direction of a force
Increase total output energy above input energy
Reduce both force and distance without a tradeoff
Eliminate the need for input work

questions.question: Which simple machine uses a rigid bar that turns around a pivot?
choices: Wedge
Screw
Lever
Inclined plane

questions.question: What is the pivot point of a lever called?
choices: Load
Effort
Axle in every case
Fulcrum

questions.question: Which simple machine is a sloped surface used to raise a load?
choices: Wheel and axle
Inclined plane
Pulley
Lever

questions.question: Which simple machine is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder?
choices: Wedge
Pulley
Screw
Lever

questions.question: Which simple machine consists of a grooved wheel guiding a rope?
choices: Pulley
Wedge
Screw
Ramp

questions.question: How is mechanical advantage calculated from forces?
choices: Output force divided by input force
Input force divided by distance
Output distance divided by time
Input force multiplied by output force

questions.question: Why does an ideal ramp reduce the force needed to lift a load?
choices: The load's gravitational weight decreases on the ramp
Output work becomes smaller than the height gain requires
The effort acts through a longer distance
The machine increases available energy without input

questions.question: Why can a single fixed pulley be useful even without multiplying force?
choices: It doubles the effort force automatically
It changes the direction of the applied force
It doubles the load's mass
It reduces the ideal input work to zero

questions.question: Why is actual machine efficiency below 100% when friction is present?
choices: Energy is destroyed inside the machine
Output work must exceed input work
Useful work includes every bit of frictional heating
Some input energy becomes thermal energy

questions.question: How can a longer effort arm help a lever lift the same load?
choices: The load's mass must decrease
The longer arm reduces torque for the same effort
Less effort force can provide the needed torque
The load arm must be longer than the effort arm

questions.question: What makes a knife blade an example of a wedge?
choices: Its handle rotates a rope
Its blade is a threaded cylinder
Its mass increases during cutting
Its sloping surfaces redirect a force to separate material

questions.question: Why does a wheel and axle offer force multiplication in some arrangements?
choices: The axle always removes the load's resistance
Forces act at different distances from a common rotation axis
All forces act at equal radii
The wheel creates more output work than input work

questions.question: What tradeoff accompanies ideal force multiplication?
choices: Greater effort distance for a smaller effort force
Greater output work than input work
A shorter effort distance for the same output work
Identical effort and load distances in every arrangement

questions.question: How does reducing friction affect a real machine's efficiency?
choices: It makes output work greater than input work
It changes the load's gravitational weight to zero
It generally increases the fraction of input work delivered usefully
It reduces useful output while input stays fixed

questions.question: A machine has input force 25 N and output force 100 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
An ideal ramp raises a 100 N load by 1 m over a 5 m slope. What effort force is needed parallel to the ramp?
choices: 5 N

questions.question: A machine receives 200 J of work and delivers 150 J of useful work. What is its efficiency?
A lever's effort arm is 3 m and load arm is 1 m. What effort balances a 60 N load, ignoring lever weight?
A compound machine contains a lever and a pulley. Which statement remains true for an ideal version?
choices: Total output work must exceed input work
More components eliminate all frictional losses
Mechanical advantages add extra energy to the system
Total output work cannot exceed input work
